single_lever_violation.note: The classifier was fundamentally retrained with completely different training data (sociology+proxy -> japanese_civics). Argmax flip rate 52.5% (probability-based 83.37%) confirms this is NOT a single-lever change. Additionally, legal training data increased 77->150.

e37_results.note: education_recall 0.4588->0.8824 (+0.4235) appears to be a massive improvement, but this experiment is INVALID due to: (1) CRITICAL label leakage: ALL 150 japanese_civics eval questions are in the training data, making pure education recall 100% (memorization, not generalization). (2) Single-lever violation: argmax flip rate 52.5% (far above 15% threshold). (3) Legal training data increased 77->150, explaining legal_recall improvement. The education_recall improvement is an artifact of memorization. This experiment cannot be used to evaluate the effectiveness of japanese_civics as an education proxy task. Next step: regenerate eval dataset excluding japanese_civics from education eval (Option A in journal analysis).

single_lever_violation.note: Argmax flip rate 20.44% exceeds the <15% threshold. Education training data doubled (150->350), causing substantial changes to the embedding space and decision boundaries. class_weight balanced recalculation also affected other domains.

e38_results.note: hybrid approach (japanese_civics + old proxy tasks) REJECTED. education_recall 0.4588->0.4000 (-0.0588) instead of improving. education_precision significantly degraded (0.5306->0.4000, p=0.0238). top1_accuracy showed no significant improvement (p=0.0748). ECE slightly worsened (0.0712->0.0862). Flip rate 20.44% indicates substantial classifier changes beyond single-lever scope. Root cause: japanese_civics addition did not improve education recall; class_weight recalculation likely contributed to degradation. Next steps: (A) class_weight=None + manual sample_weight, (B) japanese_civics-only with leakage avoidance, (C)大幅增加 handmade education problems, (D) re-evaluate education_recall baseline.

single_lever_violation.note: Argmax flip rate 4.69% (75/1600) is below the <15% threshold. Single-lever principle satisfied. Same training data, same eval dataset, same temperature calibration. The only difference is class_weight=None + manual sample_weight vs class_weight=balanced.

e39_results.note: manual sample_weight reproduction of class_weight balanced REJECTED as a hypothesis for improving education_recall. Key findings: (1) education_recall unchanged: 0.4588->0.4588 (identical). (2) medical_recall unchanged: 0.5112->0.5112 (identical). (3) top1_accuracy +0.0100 (0.6056->0.6156) but McNemar p=0.0848, not significant at alpha=0.05. (4) 75/1600 rows (4.7%) changed predictions, concentrated in history_culture (+10.12pt recall) and minor shifts elsewhere. (5) ECE slightly worsened (0.0712->0.0807). (6) Brier score slightly improved (0.6068->0.6000). (7) No BH-significant regressions or improvements in 20 per-domain metrics. Root cause: manual sample_weight with class_weight=None produces functionally equivalent effective weights to class_weight=balanced (both yield domain_weight = n_samples/(n_classes*n_domain_samples)). The 75 changed predictions are numerical noise from the solver, not a systematic improvement. The hypothesis that removing class_weight=balanced would improve education_recall is not supported by this experiment. Next steps: (A) investigate why education_recall is stuck at 0.4588 despite balanced weighting, (B) consider fundamentally different education proxy tasks or handmade education problems beyond what Iter35 tested, (C) re-evaluate whether education_recall 0.5112 is the right benchmark.

single_lever_violation.note: Argmax flip rate 52.56% (841/1600) massively exceeds <15% threshold. Full embedding model fine-tuning restructured ALL domain embeddings, not just education. 8/10 domains showed BH-significant recall regression.

e40_results.note: embedding_adaptation=setfit_education_finetune REJECTED. Key findings: (1) education_recall improved 0.4588→0.6529 (+0.1941, McNemar p=1.74e-05), but medical_recall dropped 0.5112→0.3090 (-0.2022, McNemar p=7.50e-05). (2) 14/40 (35%) of medical questions that flipped from correct to wrong now go directly to education, proving embedding space restructuring brought education and medical closer. (3) 13/20 per-domain metrics showed BH-significant regression. (4) argmax flip rate 52.56% confirms this is NOT a single-lever change. (5) ECE improved (0.0712→0.0335) but this reflects probability extremization, not calibration improvement. Root cause: SetFit/SentenceTransformer full-parameter fine-tuning cannot be confined to a single domain. Next steps: (A) adapter-only fine-tuning (LoRA-style, preserving existing infrastructure), (B) linear projection on embedding output only, (C) re-evaluate education_recall benchmark.
